services.name: Residential Epoxy Flooring
services.tagline: Seamless, waterproof floors for basements, laundry rooms, workshops, and mudrooms.
services.description: Residential epoxy isn't just for garages. In a basement, laundry room, mudroom, or hobby workshop, an epoxy floor is one of the most practical surfaces you can install — fully sealed, waterproof at the surface, resistant to spills, and easy to mop. We work directly with homeowners to choose colour, texture, and flake pattern that fits the space: a solid matte charcoal for a modern basement rec room, a warm tan flake for a mudroom that'll see muddy boots, or a metallic marbled finish for a home gym that doubles as entertaining space. Each room gets the full prep treatment — moisture test, mechanical grind, crack repair — because the biggest difference between a floor that lasts fifteen years and a floor that peels in two is the prep underneath. We fit timelines around your family: most residential rooms are drive-on done in 48 hours and back in service by the weekend.
features: Full moisture testing before scheduling
Mechanical surface prep (no shortcuts)
Choice of solid colour, flake, or metallic finishes
Matte, satin, or high-gloss topcoat
Easy-to-clean, seamless surface — no grout lines
Waterproof at the surface (ideal for basements)

Floor moisture test and crack mapping
Furniture-out, mechanical grind, crack repair
Primer coat and let cure
Decorative or solid-colour body coat
Topcoat with chosen gloss level
Walk-on next day, furniture back by end of week

faqs.q: Does it feel cold like bare concrete?
faqs.a: Yes — the surface temperature matches the concrete beneath. For basements, we often recommend pairing with area rugs or a radiant floor system if you're starting from scratch.

faqs.q: How disruptive is the install?
faqs.a: The room needs to be emptied for 48–72 hours. We bring HEPA-filtered grinders so dust stays contained, and low-odour chemistry options exist for rooms adjacent to living spaces.

faqs.q: What about moisture pushing up from below?
faqs.a: This is the biggest reason basements fail. We always test slab moisture first. If vapour emission is high, we spec a moisture-tolerant primer specifically designed to tolerate hydrostatic pressure from below.

services.name: Commercial Epoxy Flooring
services.tagline: High-traffic floors for showrooms, warehouses, retail, gyms, and auto shops.
services.description: Commercial floors have a different job than residential ones. They need to hold up to forklifts, pallet jacks, rolling retail displays, dropped weights, and the odd oil leak — all while looking presentable to customers walking in the door. Our commercial epoxy and polyaspartic systems are specified based on the actual use: a car showroom needs reflectivity and chemical resistance; a dumbbell gym needs impact resistance and sound dampening; a warehouse needs abrasion resistance and clear traffic markings. We handle everything from a 1,500 sq ft retail showroom to multi-tenant industrial facilities, with scheduling that works around your operation — overnight pours, weekend installs, and phased sections so you never have to close completely. Line striping, logos, and safety markings are integrated into the system where needed.

services.name: Polished Concrete Floors
services.tagline: Low-maintenance architectural flooring with a seamless, modern finish.
services.description: Polished concrete isn't a coating — it's a mechanical refinement of the concrete slab itself. Using progressively finer diamond-impregnated pads, we grind, hone, and polish the existing floor until it reaches the gloss level you want: a soft honed matte, a satin sheen, or a mirror polish that reflects the ceiling. Along the way, we densify the surface with lithium silicate, which fills microscopic pores and makes the final floor significantly harder and more stain-resistant than raw concrete. The result is a floor that lasts the life of the building, requires only occasional buffing to maintain, and has zero volatile chemistry — nothing to off-gas, nothing to peel. We polish floors in modern homes, retail spaces, galleries, offices, and light-industrial spaces across the GTA. The look pairs beautifully with modern or minimalist architecture, and the operating cost over fifteen years is lower than practically any other flooring option.

Lithium silicate densification for hardness and stain resistance
Choice of matte, satin, semi-gloss, or mirror finish

Optional dye for colour tint

Minimal ongoing maintenance (dust-mop + occasional buff)

process: Floor assessment: slab condition, aggregate size, existing coatings
Removal of any existing coating or adhesive residue

Final polish to desired gloss (up to 3000 grit)

idealFor: Modern homes with open-concept main floors
Any space where the slab is already in good condition

faqs.q: Can you polish an older or stained slab?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Older slabs often grind up beautifully once the top layer is removed. Deep stains or oil penetration can show through, which we document before starting so there are no surprises.

faqs.q: Does it stay shiny forever?
faqs.a: The polish holds for years with normal residential use. Commercial floors benefit from a yearly buff with a lithium polish-conditioner. If the shine ever drops, we can re-polish the top layer in a day without starting over.

faqs.q: What about radiant heating?
faqs.a: Polished concrete is excellent for radiant floors — the concrete mass stores and distributes heat beautifully, and there's no coating layer to insulate the surface.

services.name: Concrete Staining
services.tagline: Rich, variegated colour applied directly to interior concrete — no two floors identical.
services.description: Concrete staining is how you take a plain grey slab and turn it into something that looks like aged leather, weathered stone, or hand-rubbed wood. We work with both acid-based reactive stains, which chemically bond with the concrete and produce rich, variegated earthy tones, and water-based dyes, which offer a wider colour range and more predictable application. The look depends heavily on the slab underneath — curing age, finish technique, embedded aggregate — which is why no two stained floors are exactly alike. That variability is the entire appeal. We seal every stained floor with a penetrating sealer, a wax, or a clear topcoat depending on use and desired sheen. The result is a one-of-a-kind interior floor with the character of natural stone and the price point of refinishing what's already there.

faqs.q: How do I know what colour it'll end up?
faqs.a: We always do a test patch — usually a 2-foot square in a corner — so you can see how your specific slab reacts before we commit to the full floor. The character of each slab shapes the final result.

faqs.q: Will it fade?
faqs.a: Under a sealer, acid stains are permanent and don't fade. Water-based dyes have slightly less UV resistance and should be sealed with a UV-stable topcoat if there's direct sunlight on the floor.

faqs.q: What if I don't like it?
faqs.a: This is why we do test patches. If you don't like how your slab is reacting, we switch to a water-based dye or a different approach before applying to the full area.

services.name: Decorative Concrete Overlays
services.tagline: Resurface worn concrete with a stamped, troweled, or spray-textured architectural finish.
services.description: Decorative overlays are thin, polymer-modified cementitious coatings that bond to existing concrete and give you a fresh, designed surface — stamped like flagstone, troweled smooth, broom-finished, or spray-textured. Overlays are the right call when the slab is structurally sound but the surface is tired: pitted, stained beyond staining, poorly finished originally, or just dated. Instead of ripping out and re-pouring (which is expensive and disruptive), we bond a 1/8-to-1/2-inch overlay directly to what's there. The design options are broad: hand-cut flagstone patterns, European tile looks, slate textures, broom finishes, or clean modern trowel marks. Overlays can be colour-integrated or stained afterward, and we seal every overlay for durability. Interior overlays last decades indoors because they're protected from freeze-thaw.

faqs.q: Can you match a specific stone look?
faqs.a: In most cases, yes. We have texture mats and stamp patterns for popular stone types, and hand-tooling can replicate most natural patterns. Share a photo of what you're after.

faqs.q: How thick does it need to be?
faqs.a: For foot traffic indoors, 1/8 to 1/4 inch is typical. If you need to level a slab or hide significant pitting, we build thicker and feather edges to meet adjacent flooring.

faqs.q: Will it crack where the slab cracks?
faqs.a: An overlay bonds to the slab, so if the slab moves significantly, the overlay will follow. For existing cracks, we route and fill with flexible polyurethane before overlay, which minimizes crack telegraphing.

services.name: Basement Floor Coating
services.tagline: Finish your basement floor properly — sealed, decorative, and ready for everyday use.
services.description: A basement floor coating is often the most impactful upgrade you can do in a finished basement. Below-grade concrete is prone to moisture migration from below and condensation from above, and most finishing systems (vinyl plank, carpet, laminate) handle this poorly over time. A properly specified coating — epoxy, polyaspartic, or a hybrid system — is permanently bonded to the slab, waterproof at the surface, and will outlast practically any other flooring choice in that space. We moisture-test every basement slab before scheduling because moisture is the single biggest predictor of basement coating failure, and we match the primer specifically to the moisture vapour emission level we measure. The finish can be solid, decorative flake, or metallic depending on the room's purpose: subdued charcoal for a theatre room, warm tan flake for a kids' play area, metallic marbled teal for a home office with character. We've coated basement floors across every neighbourhood in the GTA, from century-old Toronto homes to new-build suburban basements.

faqs.q: What if my basement had moisture problems before?
faqs.a: We moisture-test first, always. If vapour emission is high, we spec a system that tolerates it. If there's active water intrusion, we'll flag that and recommend addressing the water source before coating.

faqs.q: Can I put furniture back right away?
faqs.a: Light furniture after 48 hours. Heavier items (sofas, treadmills, dressers) after 5 days to let the floor fully harden under load.

faqs.q: Does it feel cold?
faqs.a: Yes, same as any concrete floor. For basements where this matters, pair with area rugs over the main zones. We can also coordinate with heated-floor installers if you're starting from scratch.

services.name: Interior Concrete Resurfacing
services.tagline: Fix pitted, cracked, or worn interior concrete without demo and re-pour.
services.description: Interior concrete resurfacing is the practical middle ground between living with a tired slab and tearing it out. If your interior concrete is structurally sound but the surface is pitted, spalled, cracked, or just unattractive, resurfacing bonds a fresh cementitious or polymer layer onto what's there. The build is thinner than a full overlay — typically 1/16 to 1/8 of an inch — and is designed to restore the surface rather than create a new look. From there, the resurfaced slab can accept staining, polishing, or a decorative coating, giving you a full menu of final finishes. Resurfacing is especially useful for garage conversions, retail renovations, and basement upgrades where the original slab wasn't finished with a final use in mind. It's dramatically cheaper and less disruptive than demo and re-pour, and in most cases the finished floor is indistinguishable from new concrete.

faqs.q: Can I stain the resurfaced floor?
faqs.a: Absolutely — this is one of the most common sequences. Resurface first to level the slab, then stain or dye for colour, then seal. Great outcome, cheap compared to new concrete.

faqs.q: How do I know if my slab is sound enough?
faqs.a: We assess at the first visit — tap-test, visual inspection, and if there's doubt, a core cut. Resurfacing requires a stable substrate; if the slab is spalling or lifting, we'll flag that.

faqs.q: Is this the same as an overlay?
faqs.a: Related but different. Resurfacing restores the existing surface at a thin build. Overlays build a new decorative surface on top, often thicker and with pattern work. We'll recommend which fits your situation.

services.name: Decorative Concrete Features
services.tagline: Custom countertops, feature walls, hearths, and architectural concrete elements.
services.description: Concrete isn't just a floor — it's an architectural material, and it works beautifully on vertical surfaces, countertops, fireplace surrounds, and furniture-grade feature pieces. Our decorative concrete work covers kitchen and bath countertops with hand-honed edges, fireplace hearths and surrounds that cast in place or install as prefabricated panels, feature accent walls with hand-troweled texture, and custom pieces like floating benches or integrated sinks. Each piece is designed with the client — colour, texture, aggregate exposure, edge detail — and finished to furniture-grade standards. We work in both cast-in-place and prefabricated-panel approaches depending on access, weight, and timeline. The look fits modern, industrial, and transitional architecture equally well.

faqs.q: Will it stain from wine or oil?
faqs.a: Properly sealed concrete countertops are stain-resistant but not stain-proof. We use food-safe sealers that handle normal kitchen use well, and we re-seal annually if desired.

faqs.q: Can you match a specific colour?

services.name: Interior Stucco & Accent Walls
services.tagline: Venetian plaster, troweled stucco, and architectural accent-wall finishes.
services.description: Interior stucco and Venetian plaster are architectural finishes that bring depth, texture, and the richness of hand-trowel work to walls, ceilings, and feature zones. The look ranges from the glassy polished sheen of classical Venetian plaster to the matte troweled texture of modern limewash and the deep dimensional feel of multi-layered Marmorino. Each system is applied in multiple thin coats, worked while plastic, and burnished or textured by hand — which is why no two walls look exactly alike and why the result reads as hand-crafted rather than factory-produced. We handle feature accent walls, entire rooms, foyers, hospitality lobbies, and feature ceilings. The parent company Decor Coatings has done this work for exterior facades for years; now the same team brings it indoors for GTA homes and commercial projects.

faqs.q: Is this the same as painted texture?
faqs.a: No. Textured paint sits on the surface; plaster is a mineral finish applied in multiple thin coats and worked by hand. The depth, sheen, and feel are fundamentally different — closer to stone than to paint.

faqs.q: How long does a wall take?
faqs.a: A typical accent wall takes 2–3 days: prep and first coat on day one, second coat and burnishing on day two, final touch-up and sealing on day three.

faqs.q: Can you match a specific look?
faqs.a: Yes — share a photo or sample of what you're after, and we'll create a sample board on your actual wall before committing to the full project. This is how we dial in the exact colour and texture.

services.name: Decorative Wall Finishes
services.tagline: Hand-applied interior wall finishes — texture, movement, and depth beyond what paint can deliver.
services.description: A paint colour is one dimension. A decorative wall finish is three. Our applicators use trowel, sponge, and float techniques to build up thin, layered coats that read differently depending on light, angle, and time of day — a soft limewashed warmth in a sunlit dining room, a brushed metallic sheen in a boutique retail fitting zone, or a honed-stone matte in a modern primary bedroom. We work with hand-mixed mineral finishes, modified plasters, metallic glazes, and specialty acrylics, and we match the technique to the room's architecture and the look you want. Most finishes install over a prepared drywall or existing paint substrate — no demolition. Expect 2–4 days per room depending on finish complexity, and dust is minimal because the work is wet-trowelled, not sanded.

faqs.q: How is this different from textured paint?
faqs.a: Textured paint is a single coat with a stipple or roll pattern baked in. A decorative wall finish is multiple hand-trowelled layers, each one reacting to the previous — the depth is physical, not optical. The result reads as architectural, not decorative.

faqs.q: Can you match a reference photo?
faqs.a: Yes. Bring a photo and we'll produce a sample board on site before committing a wall. Most finishes can be tuned within a workable range for colour, sheen, and texture.

faqs.q: How do I clean it?
faqs.a: Most finishes are wipeable with a damp microfibre once fully cured (7 days). Lime and mineral finishes are the most tolerant of moisture; waxed metallics should be dusted rather than wet-cleaned.

services.name: Architectural Wall Designs
services.tagline: Custom wall compositions — panels, reveals, textures, and finishes designed as architectural features.
services.description: An architectural wall is a composed surface — not just a flat colour, not just a texture, but a planned composition of panels, reveals, insets, and finishes that reads as part of the building, not applied to it. We work with homeowners, interior designers, and architects to translate elevations into installable systems: fluted plaster panels around a fireplace, large-format concrete-look slabs forming an entry statement, raised reveals and shadow lines in a corridor, or a feature wall combining microcement with a brass inlay. The finish is only part of it — the layout, the reveal spacing, the way light grazes across the surface — these are the details that make the wall architectural rather than decorative. Timelines vary with complexity: a single-wall feature is typically 3–5 days; a multi-wall room design can take 7–10 days.

faqs.a: Routinely. Share your elevation drawings and finish schedule and we'll quote directly from your spec. We'll also raise flags early if a detail won't trowel cleanly.

faqs.q: Can the design be modified during install?

faqs.q: How does this hold up over time?

services.name: Venetian Plaster
services.tagline: Authentic lime-and-marble-dust plaster — hand-burnished to a stone-like finish.
services.description: True Venetian plaster is a lime-based plaster carrying crushed marble dust, applied in thin layers with a steel trowel and then burnished until the surface reads as honed stone. It's one of the oldest decorative wall systems — Roman villas used it, Palladio spec'd it, and it still has no modern substitute for the look. We work with traditional Italian materials (grassello, marmorino, stucco veneziano) and apply with authentic technique: three to five coats, each one skimmed thinner than the last, finished with a hard burnish and optional wax seal. The result is a surface with real depth — light pools in some spots and glides across others, the way it does on polished stone. Perfect for walls where you want permanence and gravitas, not just colour. Typically 3–5 days per room including prep.

Substrate prep — level drywall or existing plaster
Primer coat tinted to base colour
Three to five plaster coats, each thinner than the last
Burnish with steel trowel to open or close the surface
Optional wax seal and buff
idealFor: Dining room and formal living spaces
Hospitality bars, lounges, and spa interiors
Luxury retail changing rooms and brand walls

faqs.q: Does Venetian plaster work in bathrooms?
faqs.a: Yes — it's one of the oldest moisture-tolerant wall systems. Grassello with a wax seal is routinely spec'd for bathrooms, including feature walls near (not inside) showers.

faqs.q: How is it different from Venetian-style paint?
faqs.a: Paint products marketed as 'Venetian' are tinted glazes on top of a flat base. True Venetian is physical plaster — the depth is layered material, not optical trick. The difference is immediately visible under raking light.

faqs.q: Can colours be matched to a Benjamin Moore / Farrow & Ball chip?
faqs.a: Approximately. Lime plaster accepts mineral and iron-oxide tints which have their own palette — we'll produce a sample board matched as closely as possible, which may read slightly warmer or deeper than the paint chip.

services.name: Concrete Designs on Walls
services.tagline: Concrete-look wall surfaces — board-form, slab-cast appearance, or applied overlay. Industrial elegance.
services.description: A concrete wall surface — real or applied — carries a specific aesthetic: the matte, mineral honesty of raw material. We create concrete-look wall surfaces three ways. Overlay: a thin cementitious layer trowelled over existing drywall or plaster, finished to look poured. Panel: large-format precast or lightweight GFRC panels installed as wall cladding with revealed joints. Board-form: a textured overlay that captures the imprint of wood boards, mimicking the construction-joint aesthetic of poured architectural concrete. All three systems give you the look without the structural reality — a concrete wall over studs and drywall, lighter than any slab, and sealed to resist moisture and staining. Finishes range from honed smooth to raw-cast to pigmented warm tones. Typically 4–6 days per feature wall; whole-room installations take 2 weeks.
features: Overlay, panel, or board-form systems
Grey, warm-grey, charcoal, or custom pigmented
Honed-smooth, matte, or textured finishes
Lightweight — no structural change to the wall
Breathable and sealed against moisture
Revealed joints and board-form patterns on request
process: Finish, pigment, and joint pattern selection
Substrate prep — level, prime, bond-coat
Base layer trowel (overlay) or panel install (cladding)
Texture pass — board-form imprint or hand-trowel movement
Pigment stain or integral colour application
Seal with matte, satin, or honed topcoat
idealFor: Media walls and modern fireplace surrounds
Loft-style living rooms and dining spaces
Restaurant feature walls, bars, and cafes

faqs.q: Does it feel cold like real concrete?
faqs.a: The surface reads cooler than drywall because it's mineral — but it won't dramatically affect room temperature since the mass behind is still wood or steel framing.

faqs.q: Can I hang art and shelving?
faqs.a: Yes. Panel systems typically mount into stud bays; overlays retain the stud / blocking anchor points below. Flag locations in advance so we can note where sealant should be reinforced.

faqs.q: How does it compare in cost to actual concrete?
faqs.a: Dramatically cheaper, lighter, and installable in finished homes without structural work. Also fully reversible — a future owner can skim and paint over if they want a different look.

services.name: Decorative Interior Floor Coatings
services.tagline: Floor coatings designed as finished interiors — metallic, flake, quartz, and designer blend systems.
services.description: A decorative floor coating isn't a utility surface — it's a floor you'd choose over hardwood or tile for the aesthetic. We work with metallic epoxies that pool and marble under the trowel, acrylic quartz systems that read like terrazzo, high-gloss designer flakes in custom colour blends, and matte designer-pigmented urethanes that look like honed concrete. These systems are a step up from standard epoxy or garage flooring: tighter prep, more hands-on application, and finish options tuned for interior living spaces instead of utility rooms. Typical installations run 3–5 days including cure, with the room usable (foot traffic) the day after the final coat and fully loaded a week later.
features: Metallic epoxy with marbled movement
Acrylic quartz / terrazzo-look systems
Designer flake blends — custom palette
Pigmented urethane with honed-concrete look
Matte, satin, or high-gloss topcoat
Seamless, hypoallergenic, allergen-friendly surface
process: In-home consultation and sample board
Moisture test and substrate assessment
Mechanical surface prep (diamond grind)
Primer coat and crack repair
Decorative body coat (metallic, flake, quartz, or pigmented)
Topcoat with chosen sheen
Walk-on next day, full load after one week

faqs.q: How is this different from regular epoxy?
faqs.a: Standard epoxy is a utility surface — one base coat, one topcoat, solid colour or basic flake. Decorative systems use metallic resins, quartz aggregate, or designer flake blends that are specifically chosen for how they read as a finished floor in a living space.

faqs.q: Does it feel softer than tile?
faqs.a: Marginally — the resin layer has slight give compared to tile or stone. It's warmer underfoot than concrete, cooler than wood.

faqs.q: How well does it hold up with pets?
faqs.a: Very well. Pet nails don't mark the topcoat (satin or matte hide any micro-scratches best), spills wipe up, and the surface is naturally antimicrobial after cure.

services.name: Microcement
services.tagline: Seamless cementitious finish for floors, walls, bathrooms, and kitchens — 2–3mm thick, no joints.
services.description: Microcement is the finish that lets you specify concrete anywhere — bathroom walls, shower surrounds, kitchen counters, floors, feature walls, even furniture — without the weight, structural demand, or joints of actual concrete. It's a polymer-modified cementitious coating applied in two to three thin layers (total thickness 2–3 mm) over almost any substrate: drywall, existing tile, plywood, backer-board, concrete. The result is a seamless, waterproof, mineral surface that reads as honed concrete — matte, cool, with subtle hand-trowelled movement. Microcement has transformed European bathroom and kitchen design in the last decade because it eliminates grout lines entirely, which is why Toronto and GTA interior designers increasingly spec it. We install authentic imported systems (Topciment, Microbeton class) with the full prep: substrate consolidation, mesh reinforcement at joints, two base coats, two finish coats, and a two-part sealer rated for wet environments. Typical bathroom: 5–7 days including cure.
features: 2–3 mm thick — installs over tile, drywall, concrete, plywood
Fully seamless — no grout lines anywhere
Fully waterproof when sealed — bathrooms, showers, kitchens
Mineral, matte finish — reads as honed concrete
Pigmentable to any palette (warm, cool, neutral)
Walls, floors, counters, built-ins — same system
process: Substrate inspection and sample board
Prep — clean, consolidate, mesh at joints
Primer coat for substrate type
Two base coats, each hand-trowelled and sanded
Two finish coats — colour and movement
Two-part sealer (urethane or epoxy) rated for the space
Final buff and acceptance walkthrough
idealFor: Bathroom walls, floors, and shower surrounds
Retail and hospitality bars and counters

faqs.q: Will microcement crack?
faqs.a: If the substrate moves, any surface will crack — microcement, tile, hardwood. The install protocol specifically addresses this: mesh reinforcement over joints and transitions, consolidation of soft substrates, and controlled curing. Properly installed, it holds up for decades.

faqs.q: Is it slippery when wet?
faqs.a: The topcoat sheen determines slip. Bathrooms and showers get a matte textured topcoat that meets Canadian bathroom slip-rating standards. High-gloss microcement would be slippery in a shower — we don't install it there.

faqs.q: Can microcement go over existing tile?
faqs.a: Yes — this is one of its biggest advantages. We skim the grout lines flat with a consolidating primer, bond directly to the tile, then build up the microcement system. No demolition needed.
